findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

1) The hand sink by the walk in cooler would not dispense paper towels at the time of the inspection. 2) The hand sink at the front service counter would not dispense paper towels at the time of the inspection. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and paper towels placed next to the sinks to correct the violation. Ensure that the hand sinks are supplied with useable hand drying provisions at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

The hand sink by the walk in cooler was observed pulling away from the wall which produced a gap that was not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to have resealed prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all wall attachments provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface at all times.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dust on the walk-in cooler fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed the single-use utensils at the front customer counter were stored with the food contact surfaces facing upwards. The PIC was educated and the utensils were inverted during the inspection. Ensure that single-use utensils are always stored with the handles facing outwards to avoid contaminating food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the containers holding clean dishes on the shelving across from the dish machine had an accumulation of food residue and other debris on the bottom. The PIC was informed and the containers were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. When the PIC was notified they noticed that the empty sanitizer bucket that an employee was supposed to change last night was still not changed. During the inspection a new sanitizer bucket was attached and the dish machine tested at 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that the dish machine is tested on a regular basis to ensure that food-contact surfaces are being sanitized before use.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed a paddle drying behind the faucet of the triple sink. This position poses a risk of contamination from dirty water splashes or food debris. The PIC moved the paddle into a new position during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces remain clean to sight and touch.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer buckets were testing at 0 ppm at the start of the inspection. The PIC said the buckets were made this morning and needed to be changed. They were dumped and remade during the inspection. After being re-made they were testing at 700 ppm (sink and sanitizer cleaner). Ensure that chemical sanitizers meet the proper criteria. Also ensure that sanitizer buckets are tested on a regular basis and re-made as needed.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop container at the front soda machine had an accumulation of soil residues on the bottom. The ice scoop and container were removed from service to be cleaned. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following physical facilities need to be repaired: (1) The cove base top that is becoming de-attached from the wall below the drive through window; and (2) The hole in the wall from the old soda line to the left of the drive through soda machine. Ensure that physical families are repaired by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FOUR TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION. The caulking behind the rinsing table to the left of the dish machine is soiled and missing in the middle. All areas of the facility subject to food/water must be constructed of surfaces which are smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable. The high amount of water usage in this location requires the caulking be maintained and replaced frequently. Due to the amount of repeat violations the inspector will return on 11/13/2024 to ensure the caulking has been replaced. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mop heads stored on the mop sink basin. The PIC was educated and the mop heads were removed for laundering. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the front hand sink did not have paper towels. An employee re-filled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that all hand skinks have paper towels available. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed some of the utensils at the front of the facility were stored inverted with the food contact surface facing outwards. There were also some utensils which were falling out of the container due to lack of space. An employee corrected the storage of the utensils during the inspection. Ensure utensils are always stored correctly to prevent contamination.

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: (1) Food debris on the bottom of containers holding utensils and other items in the dish washing area; (2) Accumulated food debris on the outside and within cracks of the dishwasher; and (3) Soil and dust on the green shelving in the dish area. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The caulking behind the left side of the dish machine is soiled and in need of cleaning/replacing. All areas of the facility subject to food/water must be constructed of surfaces which are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that all surfaces in these areas are corrected by the next routine inspection. THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the PIC did not have copies available of food handler certificates for employees. Ensure that all employees complete the food handler training within 30 days of hire and copies of the certificates are kept in the facility. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Observed that none of the managers have done their allergen awareness training. Ensure that all certified service sanitation managers obtain their basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days of employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

As the inspection began, a step ladder was observed in front of the hand sink between the drive thru and main prep areas. The ladder was removed immediately to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are easily accessible at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple pans on the storage racks are observed with baked on bag wrappers, food debris or sticker residues. The PICs were shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that all equipment and utensils are completely cleaned prior to storage. Education with the dish washers is highly suggested moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket next to the prep line is heavily soiled and not registering on the inspector’s test strips. The label on the bucket also suggested that it may have needed replacing prior to observation as well. The bucket was remade during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

1) The northernmost set of cabinets in the front register area have a sticky residue accumulating from the tea and lemonade. The floor next to these cabinets is also soiled with the same residue as is the inside of the door. 2) Under the soda machine/ice bin in the drive thru there is an accumulation of soda syrup spray at the back of the cabinet. 3) Mold growth observed on the wall behind the dish sink. These areas must be clean to sight and touch at the next routine inspection. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces of the facility are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM 08/21/2023.

There are still numerous drain flies near the drains in the NE corner of the kitchen around the triple sink and ice machine. No change from 08/24. No additional drain cleaning/treatment. Ensure that drains are cleaned and treated and that drain flies are drastically reduced by the next follow-up in 10-days (approximately). Follow-up is issued for Wednesday 9/6/2023.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Inspector observed corrective actions taken regarding hand washing at the facility to be inadequate. Management was instructed that they must DEMONSTRATE proper procedure for handwashing. Person-in-charge has been simply telling staff they they must follow steps 1-6 on the posted hand washing instructions. Pointing out where to find proper procedure is not sufficient training and/or correction for staff to take corrective actions. Further, by pushing the responsibility of training off and instructing staff to self-train reduced employee morale and motivation to follow procedure. They will not take the policy seriously if they feel management does not take the policy seriously. As such, a 2nd follow-up is issued for this violation to evaluate training practices to ensure they are adequate for staff to adopt required practices. Ensure that the person-in-charge is training staff and demonstrating proper procedure, not simply directing employees where to find it and have them read it on their own.

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
On arrival, two staff members and two managers were present. Both staff members despite inspector presence required coaching to properly wash their hands. The first staff member washed hands for 20 seconds but failed to use a barrier. The 2nd staff member failed to wash for 20 seconds and failed to use a barrier. Lastly, a third employee arrived at the facility for work and was instructed by person-in-charge to wash hands. This employee failed to wash for 20-seconds twice and failed to use a barrier twice. Ensure that ALL staff are washing hands using proper PROCEDURE at proper FREQUENCY.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 08/08/2022.

The facility has several priority/priority foundation violations and repeat violations from prior inspections. Person-in-charge was unable to answer basic questions pertaining to food code requirements. Proper training must occur by store management immediately and consistently for ALL staff to ensure compliance and prevent further enforcement actions at this facility. 

A follow-up is being issued for 09/15/2023 to ensure all priority/priority foundation violations have been effectively corrected.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOALTION FROM 8/8/2022.

Inspector did not observe ANY hand washing over the course of the inspection. One hand sink in the kitchen was blocked for the duration of the inspection. The second hand sink at the front of the kitchen was dry at the beginning and end of the inspection. Person-in-charge was unsure of hand washing policy at the store level and unsure of food code requirements for hand washing. Training must occur immediately to ensure all staff are washing hands at proper intervals. A 3-day follow-up is issued for 8/21/2023 to evaluate hand washing at that time.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The rear hand washing sink of the facility was blocked with the lid to a container and had mop buckets sitting in front of it. Hand sinks must be easily accessible at ALL times to facilitate frequent use by employees. Ensure that hand sinks remain stocked and accessible and at all times. A follow-up is issued for 08/28/2023. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a can of aerosol insecticide labeled as hazardous via means of ingestion and skin contact sitting on the counter next to the tea dispenser at the drive thru area. The can of insecticide was removed during the inspection. Corrected on site. Ensure that all hazardous substances are stored away from food and in a manner which prevents contamination of food and/or food contact surfaces. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a loosely estimated 50 drain flies around the northwest corner of the kitchen. The drain flies are a repeat concern per person-in-charge. A hanging fly bait trap is hung but does not appear to be trapping flies. The flies are predominantly located near the drain underneat the triple sink and the drain in front of the ice bin as well as siting on the bucket of cleaner and the underside of the triple sink itself. The facility must be maintained free of insects at all times. Contact third party pest control to treat the flies and develop a prevention program moving froward. Eliminate harborage conditions in the facility by cleaning drains, using enzymatic cleaners in the drains, and ensuring that all areas of the facility subject to moisture remain clean at ALL times. 

A follow-up is issued for 08/28/2023 to check on the elimination of insects and harborage conditions. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Potato salad is stored in the reach-in cooler along the west wall of the kitchen without being covered. Ensure that stored foods are covered at all times to prevent contamination. Correct by the next routine inspection. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTIONS DATED 08/08/2023 AND 03/02/2022.

An in-use knife at the middle prep cooler of the kitchen (the functioning one) was stored with the food contact surface of the knife resting on the soiled, dusty top surface of the cooler. In-use utensils must be cleaned and stored on cleaned and sanitizer surfaces. Ensure that in-use utensils are stored properly by the next routine inspection.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Cleaned silverware was stored in a manner which appears to be thrown into the container with utensilves hanging out of the container in all directions. Silverware must be stored in a single direction with handles out to prevent contact with food-contact surfaces. Ensure that all utensils are stored properly by the next routine inspection. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION*.

Inspector observed the following equipment in need of repair:
- *cabinets along the front line are missing handles
- the middle prep cooler (functioning and non-functioning) is missing a handle

Ensure that equipment is in good repair by the next routine inspection. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTIONS DATED 8/8/2022 AND 2/21/2023

Inspector observed the following soiled nonfood-contact surfaces:
- The northernmost set of cabinets in font register area have a large amount of sticky residue accumulating from the tea and lemonade to the point that wiping with sani cloths was not effective at remove the sticky residue. The floor next to these cabinets is also soiled with the same residue as is the wall behind the inside of the cabinets which is bare drywall and not wood.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 2/21/2023.

Inspector observed the following areas needing repair/replacement:
- Holes in the FRP board in the dining room need sealed.
- Molded caulking behind the dish sink must be replaced.
- Heavily soiled bare drywall at the back of the cabinets under the coffee/tea/lemonade staion must be sealed and any upper portion of the counter where food/moisture may enter must be sealed. 

All areas of the facility subject to food/water must be constructed of surfaces which are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that all surfaces in these areas are corrected by the next routine inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The mop sink is completely disorganized, soiled and overloaed with equipment. Maintenance tools including mops, squeegees, brooms are all stored on the wet, soiled floor of this sink. There is no means of effectively finding and/or storing this equipment in or near the mop sink. Wet mop heads are on the floor and draped over the nearby half wall, neither of which are appropriate for preventing contamination and microbial growth. Clean the mop sink. Store all maintenance items properly. Provide a means of storing maintenance items properly. Ensure that the mop sink is corrected by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion
findings.comment:
Inspector was standing in the kitchen observing an employee washing hands who was simultaneously carrying on a conversation with another employee. Inspector overheard the employee tell the other employee that he was “puking all over the place” the day prior and was “sick as hell yesterday”. Inspector discussed sick policy with operator. The facility has their own sick policy which is more stringent than requirements imposed by 2017 FDA Code requiring 48 hours symptom free of vomiting. As such, employee was sent home. All employees must be aware of and adhere to the reporting requirements for the required symptoms and diagnoses and must report those symptoms immediately to their supervisor. Person-in-charge is responsible for ensuring compliance with reporting requirements and enforcing restriction and exclusion rules. The violation was corrected immediately by sending the employee home and no follow-up is required at this time. 

2-201.11: (D) PIC shall exclude or restrict as required. (F) A FOOD EMPLOYEE shall comply with restrictions/exclusions.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee standing immediately outside the back door smoking a cigarette. Smoke blew into the facility multiple times while employee was smoking. Person-in-charge was notified and immediately took corrective action. Corrected on site. Ensure that all employees are aware of designated smoking areas and are aware of smoke free Illinois requirements. No follow-up required at this time. 

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The metal cabinets at the front drive thru area were heavily soiled with residue and debris and contained single-serve items, personal items, mouse traps, and other refuse. The cabinets were immediately cleaned and were clean to sight and touch during the inspection. Corrected on site. Ensure that non-food-contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to preclude the accumulation of residue and debris. No follow-up required. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The dish sink, vegetable sink, and both hand sinks in the kitchen are observed to have missing/deteriorating/molding caulking between the rear of the sink and the wall. This area is subject to large amounts of moisture and counters are immovable. Sinks must be caulked to create a surface which is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that all surfaces throughout the facility are smooth and easily cleanable and if subject to food and moisture are non-absorbent. 

**This is a repeat violation from the previous inspection.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The cabinets along the front service line have several missing handles and a missing door. These cabinets store single use and single service items which are stored in cabinets to prevent contamination. Ensure that cabinet doors are repaired to allow for proper function. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: Employees do not all have food handler certificates. PIC states that these are in progress but they are outside the 30 day window post-hire to get the certification. Ensure that all food handling employees obtain their food handlers certificate.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed a mop stored in a dirty bucket. The mop was moved to the mop sink during the inspection but was stored head down on the group in the mop sink. Explained to the PIC proper storage of mops and the need to get clips fixed to hang mops properly. PIC understands and hung mops inverted along the wall as required during the inspection. Corrected on site.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Caulking around the cleaning sink where dishes are cleaned prior to going to the dish machine was observed to be molded and deteriorating. Replace caulking to ensure that the junction of the sink and wall is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Several non-food contact surfaces throughout the facility were observed to be soiled. Ensure that cleaning is done throughout the facility especially in areas such as but not limited to storage containers for utensils, underneath lids of prep coolers, and underneath coolers to prevent the accumulation of soil and debris.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed plastic single-use spoons and forks on the front line stored in soiled containers. Also observed single use sandwich toothpicks stored on soiled surfaces. Ensure that all single-use items are stored in cleaned and sanitized containers.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: An ice scoop on the front line was observed to be sitting in a storage container with visibly soiled water at the base of the container directly contacting the food-contact surface. Ensure that all in-use utensils are stored in a cleaned and sanitized location to prevent contamination.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: American cheese, pepper jack cheese, sauerkraut and other items in cold-holding were noted to have temperatures as high as 51 degrees. After speaking with PIC, it was determined that these items came from the walk in cooler. Upon inspection, the same items in the walk-in cooler were approximately 38 degrees. The temperature had increased from being in the walk-in cooler to cold-holding. The food had been in the critical temperature range for approximately 2 hours. PIC replaced missing containers to maintain cold air in the cooler and temperatures of these items were rechecked.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee washing hands and using the paper towel to turn off the faucet prior to drying hands with the same paper towel. Discussed with PIC and hands were washed appropriately. Ensure that all employees are washing their hands with the proper procedures and use the paper towel to dry hands PRIOR to using it as a barrier to turn off the faucet.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed a food employee preparing RTE sandwiches with gloves on but failing to wash hands in between activities and touching their face. Corrected on site. Hands were not washed for an adequate amount of time before returning to food preparation and employee touched her face again before grabbing gloves to prepare food. Ensure that ALL employees are aware of proper hand washing procedures and when to wash hands including any time gloves become contaminated and before putting new gloves on. Education was held with PIC and employees washed hands properly during inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: Establishment had several priority/priority foundation items during the inspection. PIC was observed to follow improper hand washing procedures by drying hands with a soiled paper towel used as a barrier. These issues were discussed with PIC and PIC understands the need for compliance and is actively correcting violations.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The container used for the ice scoop in the drive thru area is observed with approximately 1/2 inch of water in the bottom. The water is observed with small floating items in it. Discussed with the PIC and the container and scoop were moved to dish for cleaning. A fresh scoop and container were moved to the drive through for service.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

Single service items in the front are observed stored in containers with food debris in the bottom (where the food contact parts are resting). Inspector discussed with the PIC and the containers were moved to dish for cleaning. Clean containers were retrieved to replace them.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Presence of mold along the baffle of dish machine attached to the wall. Keep these areas free of debris and mold accumulation. Will follow up at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed front handwashing station without paper towels. Ensure all handwashing stations have all necessary items during all hour operations. Corrected. Towels have been replaced. Reference 6-301.12

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed potato salad and cut melon to be greater than or equal to 50F (probed). Ensure all cold-held TCS foods are maintained at 41F or below. Corrected. Cold holding unit was turned on and food was discarded.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Observed ice scoop to be sitting in soiled water. Ensure ice scoop is placed in clean area to prevent potential cross-contamination. Corrected. Ice scoop and container were cleaned. If ice scoop is placed in container, ensure container is free of debris and any residue during all times of operation. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed black residue present on lid of ice bin located in front near cash registers. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed to prevent any build-up. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed bag of frozen vegetables being thawed in handsink. Ensure handwashing is used for handwashing only. Corrected. Handsink will be cleaned. Education provided. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed knife to be in between soiled table and prep table. Ensure equipment is placed in manner to prevent potential cross contamination. Corrected. Education provided. Knife has been removed from area and will be properly cleaned.  
Observed ice scoops near all soda dispensers to be in water with physical contaminates present. Ensure scoops are placed in clean areas. Corrected. All scoops will be cleaned. Education provided. 
Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed scoop handle to be touching sugar. Ensure proper storage occurs for all in-use equipment. Corrected. Proper storage position has been implemented. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed two ice scoops to be placed in containers filled with water with visible accumulation. Observed lemonade dispenser in front area soiled with black residue. Observed knife in knife rack to be soiled. Ensure all food equipment is cleaned as needed. Clean soiled food equipment. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed three different coolers to have food above 41F. 1) Prep Cooler near dishwasher appears to be in bad repair. Cut melon and cut tomato were measured at 49F-probed. 2) Cooler (holding sauces and condiments) next to prep cooler near dishwasher was observed to be in disrepair. Cabbage/kale mix was 49F-probed. 3) Prep Cooler near vegetable sink appears to be in bad repair. Turkey was measured at 49F-probed. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).
Corrective Action. For all three coolers, PIC stated products were placed in various times. Prep Cooler near dishwasher had TCS foods placed in cooler around 1430. Products will be used or discarded by closing. Kale/Cabbage mix was placed in cooler around ~930. Product will be discarded at 1700. Prep Cooler near vegetable sink was stocked ~30 minutes ago. All TCS foods will be discarded by closing. Store closes at 2100.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: REPEAT #1 Observed accumulation of ice on floor of walk-in freezer. Ensure all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
REPEAT #1 Observed no CFM to have food allergen training. Ensure all CFMs in Class I category facilities have food allergen training. 
Reference PA 100-0367.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No evidence of CFM is present during time of operation. CFM must be present during all hours of operation. Documentation must be accessible during time of inspection.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed handsink to be blocked by cart. Observed other handsink to have dirty rag inside sink. Ensure handwashing stations are always accessible during operation. Ensure handsinks are for handwashing only. Education provided.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by cart . Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. (Pf) Food employee dumped dirty towel iton the hand sink in the kitchen area. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed ice handle to be placed in container when not in use. Container was filled with water holding visible particles. Ensure ice handle is placed in clean container. Corrected. Container and ice handle were removed to be cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed in-use utensil handle in prep cooler-F to be touching food. Ensure proper storage occurs with in-use utensils.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly in prep line . Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 ?F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed soil debris near soda lines in back of kitchen, walk-in freezer, and throughout floor of facility. Clean floors and areas with excess accumulation of soilage.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on several areas. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: No individual has food allergen certificate in facility. PIC must have food allergen training for category I facilities.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Obeserved black debris build-up on the nozzles of two of three soda dispensing machines. Soda nozzles must be cleaned as needed to prevent build up and potential cross-contamination. Clean soda nozzles. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed utensil handle touching sugar in a bin labeled "sugar". Utensils must be placed in appropriate manner to prevent potential cross-contamination. store utensil in appropriate manner. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed black debris in grill surface of panini press. Clean grill atleast once a day to prevent build-up. 
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed utensils to be placed in random order that allowed handle and contact surface to be touching. All utensils must be placed in manner to prevent potential cross-contamination. Reorganize knives in appropriate manner.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 10+ drain flies present in facility. No pests can be present in facility. Remove pests harboring in facility. Corrective Action: PIC stated company came and treated drains yesterday. White powder was present around drains. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed walk-in cooler to have standing water. 
2) Observed walk-in freezer to have box of cookies open and on floor.
Clean the floors and discard cookies.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
